title: Three-up hero angles — internal brief
body:
Purpose
Quick internal brief: 3 distinct homepage hero directions (A/B/C) we want to validate with live traffic and an email nurture flow. This doc collects candidate headlines, subheads, three supporting bullets, microcopy hooks, competitive claims to test (explicit vs implicit), and metrics to judge success. Keep this loose — we will iterate after first batch of data.

Context & objective
- Audience: engineers and ML/platform leads evaluating inference for production (self-serve funnel primary), plus startup founders exploring hosted API.
- Problem we solve (core): predictable, economical LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Production constraints > model novelty.
- Objective: pick hero that maximizes mid-funnel activation (first API call + sample workload), improves click-to-signup by 8% vs baseline, and reduces homepage bounce for evaluation personas.

Guiding principles for copy
- Engineer-first language: concrete levers (latency, cost, SLAs), not marketing fluff.
- Signal production-readiness: mention observability, rollouts, dedicated/private options without jargon overload.
- Short, scannable: headline (6–8 words), subhead (18–30 words), three bullets (single-line). CTA variations: Try API | Reserve capacity | Get pricing.

Hero Angle A — Latency & reliability first (hypothesis: enterprise/platform buyers)
- Headline candidate: "Predictable latency. Production-grade inference."
- Subhead candidate: "Ship LLM features with consistent latency and automatic fallbacks across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Bullets: ["SLA-backed dedicated pools and burst capacity","Smart routing with failover to compatible model variants","Token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Console"]
- Microcopy: "Latency SLOs from 10ms–200ms depending on model and size; automatic fallback keeps apps online."
- CTA: "See latency benchmarks" / "Talk to sales"
- Competitive claim to test: explicit SLA mention vs implicit reliability claim.

Hero Angle B — Cost & control first (hypothesis: mid-market and cost-conscious teams)
- Headline candidate: "Lower per-token cost without rebuilding inference ops"
- Subhead candidate: "Batching, KV caching, and smart model routing that cut execution cost while preserving output quality."
- Bullets: ["Automated batching and prefix caching","Quantization and model recommendations per workload","Dedicated capacity for predictable unit economics"]
- Microcopy: "Switch between hosted and reserved capacity with the same API and rollout controls."
- CTA: "Estimate savings" / "Run a free cost analysis"
- Competitive claim to test: show % cost delta vs big cloud endpoints (approx numbers OK for experiment) vs qualitative claim "lower operational overhead."

Hero Angle C — Developer velocity & unified runtime (hypothesis: startups/engineers who value DX)
- Headline candidate: "One API. Multiple deployment modes. Zero surprises."
- Subhead candidate: "Same SDKs, rollout controls, and observability across hosted, dedicated, and private — so engineering teams move faster."
- Bullets: ["Consistent API for gen, chat, embeddings","Canary rollouts, A/B test, automatic fallback","Per-request tracing and prompt-level evals"]
- Microcopy: "Plug into SDKs and get token-level cost visibility in minutes."
- CTA: "Start free" / "Try the SDK"
- Competitive claim to test: emphasis on unified experience vs cloud vendor lock-in.

Secondary micro-variants (small copy swaps to run as microtests)
- Replace "Zero surprises" with "Zero environment drift" or "Zero inference surprises" to see impact.
- Subhead tone tests: technical (metrics, e.g., "10–50ms median response") vs benefits ("ship features faster").
- CTA language: action specificity test ("Start free" vs "Try the SDK" vs "Estimate savings").

Proof points / supporting links to surface on hero or immediately below
- Short stat row idea: "<model> verified throughput: 8k tokens/sec per GPU | 99.9% regional uptime | avg latency 40ms (p50, gpt-small)" — all claims to link to a performance page with methodology.
- Customer logo line: 6 logos + 1 short quote focused on reliability or cost.
- Quick bullets for why: serving runtime optimizations, kernel selection, caching & batching.

Competitive framing — what to call out in subcopy or FAQ
- Against managed cloud endpoints: emphasize specialized inference runtime, cost controls (batching/caching), and model/router fallbacks.
- Against inference-only runtimes: emphasize unified control plane + hosted & dedicated offering and enterprise SLAs.
- Against pure LLM API vendors: emphasize production economics and deployment options (private + on-prem).

Experiment plan (MVP)
- Test matrix: 3 hero angles x 2 CTAs x 2 micro-subheads = 12 variants. Run purely on self-serve funnel (US traffic, developer persona heuristics) for 3 weeks.
- Measure: primary = activation (API key created + first successful call with sample prompt within 7 days). Secondary = click-to-signup, time-on-page, bounce rate, demo request.
- Minimum detectable effect target: +8% activation over current baseline within experiment.
- Traffic allocation: 70% control (current hero) / 30% experiment (even split across 12) for initial sanity; flip after signal.
- Ramp plan: collect first-week heuristics (qualitative via session replays + heatmaps), then optimize top 2 winners and re-run.

Implementation notes for PM/Eng/Design
- Assets needed: 3 hero art directions (engineering-focused imagery, simplified infra diagrams, or clean product screenshots), one stat-row component with source links, one short testimonial.
- Quick copy blocks to hand off to dev: headlines, subheads, bullets, alt CTAs, microcopy for performance stat tooltip. Provide both technical and marketing variants.
- Analytics: track event names: hero_variant_shown, hero_cta_click, signup_start, api_key_created, first_api_call_success. Ensure infra tags map to GA/Amplitude.

Open questions / risks
- Should we call out specific numbers (latency/cost %) in hero or keep them on linked page? Risk: numbers may vary across models/hardware and could cause trust issues if not properly qualified.
- Naming: "Redwood Inference" should be used sparingly in hero; use product-first phrasing for readability.
- Compliance messaging: if we push Private mentions in hero, could confuse small teams; consider showing Private as a secondary link.

Next steps / owners
- Design: Miguel Torres — produce 3 hero art comps by 2026-02-25.
- Analytics/Eng: Lena Zhang — implement event tracking + experiment config by 2026-03-01.
- Content: Aisha Patel (owner) + Jordan Lee — finalize microcopy and experiment variants by 2026-03-03.
- Sales enablement: Samir Rao — prepare one-pager on SLA and capacity options for linked page by 2026-03-07.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic; aim to surface what engineers care about quickly. Please comment inline in Confluence-1234 rather than proposing additional headline variants here — we want to keep the matrix manageable.

Rough appendix (quick alternative lines to copy/paste into variants)
- Alt headline A1: "Inference that keeps your app online, even under load"
- Alt headline B1: "Cut inference spend without sacrificing quality"
- Alt headline C1: "One developer API for every production environment"
- Micro CTA alt list: "Estimate cost", "Start free", "See benchmarks", "Contact sales"

End.
